confirmed: The source is the J-STAGE advance publication accepted before copyediting, publicized 2025/11/28, DOI 10.1587/transinf.2025DKP0002; the PDF contains 10 pages including its cover, and its title and authors match the form. The full markdown and all PDF pages were read, including references and biographies; no appendix or supplementary-material notice appears (PDF p. 1, cover; p. 2, title/byline; pp. 9-10, references/biographies).

One within-person experiment is reported. Randomization concerns CG1/CG2 topic schedules, each N = 12; the AI-condition sequence is A, B, B, C for both groups. Thus quasi_people, observational context, criterion_1 not_met, and has_randomized_people_study = false are supported under the codebook rule requiring randomized condition order (PDF p. 3, Section 3 and Tables 1-2).

The reported experimental sample is 24 people, with 19 males and 5 females, mean age 24.8 years (SD = 2.3), paid 2,600 JPY. Two additional evaluators rated the ideas and are separate from the brainstorming sample; the sample is below 50 regardless of unreported analysis exclusions (PDF p. 2, Summary; p. 4, Section 3.1).

GPT-4o mini was provided through AI by Zapier as a Slack agent, returning three ideas per prompt; its prompts and replies were shared in Condition B, and use was unrestricted. The four brainstorming topics, 15-minute rounds, and approximately two-hour session match the form (PDF p. 3, Section 3; p. 4, Sections 3.2-3.4).

All A-versus-B originality statistics in S1-O1 match Table 3: Originality: A M = 3.31 (SD 0.44) vs B M = 3.18 (SD 0.90); U = 37.5, Z = 0.58, p = .60, r = .14. All B-versus-C originality statistics in that same reported string also match Table 5: Originality: B M = 3.94 (SD 0.79) vs C M = 3.19 (SD 1.07); W = 64.0, Z = -2.03, p = .04*, r = -.43. Their placement and analysis unit require the correction above (PDF pp. 5 and 7, Tables 3 and 5).

All S1-O2 reported statistics match Table 3: Number of ideas: A M = 17.40 (SD 7.20) vs B M = 8.10 (SD 7.10); U = 54.0, Z = 2.32, p = .02*, r = .58. The form correctly notes that Section 4.1 instead prints Z = 2.31 (PDF p. 5, Table 3 and Section 4.1).

All S1-O3 reported statistics match Table 3: Similarity: A M = 0.57 (SD 0.08) vs B M = 0.46 (SD 0.17); U = 41.0, Z = 0.95, p = .37, r = .24. The statement that higher similarity scores mean more similar ideas is correct (PDF p. 4, Section 3.5; p. 5, Table 3).

The one-line finding correctly reproduces the idea-count means 8.10 versus 17.40, U = 54.0 and p = .02; originality means 3.18 versus 3.31 and p = .60; and similarity means 0.46 versus 0.57 and p = .37. Its n = 24 is supported as the reported overall sample, with analyzed-count limitations described above (PDF p. 2, Summary; p. 5, Table 3).

Creativity and similarity were scored on human-generated output, so criterion_3 is met; core exclusion is supported by the fixed condition order and the sample below 50. This is not a synthesis, and the empty synthesis fields are appropriate (PDF pp. 3-5, Sections 3-4.1; p. 7, Table 5).
summary: The fixed condition order supports quasi_people/observational classification and no qualifying randomized AI-assistance study; the reported sample was 24 people. All reported statistics and the one-line finding match the PDF, but counts need qualification, student status is unconfirmed, and omitted outcomes, analysis units, and measurement details need correction.
